comments.note: api-knowledge.test.ts lines 244–247 and 252–255: each AC test uses two consecutive rejects.toMatchObject assertions — first .toThrow(ApiError), then .toMatchObject({ code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR' }). The second assertion already validates the error shape sufficiently (it would fail if the thrown value were not an ApiError-like object). A single rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR' }) per test would be cleaner, though the current dual-assertion is not wrong. Not worth a rework cycle; flag for future cleanup.

The let scope variable pattern (api-knowledge.ts lines 184–191) works well for this case. If additional handlers require similar scope-or-undefined guards in the future, extracting to a shared parseOptionalScope(raw: string | undefined): 'global' | 'repository' | undefined helper would eliminate duplication. No action needed now — valid for a future DRY pass if the pattern recurs.
